saints.name: St. Porphyry of Gaza
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A monk of the Egyptian desert made bishop of pagan Gaza, who by prayer and patience won that stubborn city for Christ…
biography: Porphyry, born about 347 at Thessalonica, gave up his wealth for the monastic life in the Egyptian desert and at Jerusalem, and about 395 was made bishop of Gaza, a city still fiercely devoted to its idols. His life, written by his deacon Mark, tells how he labored amid opposition for the conversion of the people.

With imperial help the pagan temples were at last closed and the great shrine of Marnas destroyed, and on its site Porphyry raised a Christian church. By his death in 420 the faith had taken firm root in Gaza.
saints.knownFor: The conversion of pagan Gaza to the Christian faith.

sources.text: Mark the Deacon, Life of St. Porphyry of Gaza (public-domain translation)
